title: IC Pin Numbering and Notch Orientation

zones.label: notch
zones.summary: This notch marks Pin 1 — always start counting here, going counter-clockwise.
facts: Every DIP chip has one: a semicircular cut, a dimple, or both, at one end of the package.
Hold the chip so the notch is on your left, then pin 1 is the first pin along the bottom edge.
If a chip has no notch, look for a small dot pressed into the plastic beside pin 1.

zones.summary: Pin 1: the first pin counter-clockwise from the notch. On a 555 this is ground.
facts: Position: 0 pins counter-clockwise from the notch — it is the starting point.
555 function: GND, the negative supply connection.
Insert the chip backwards and this pin lands where pin 5 belongs.

zones.summary: Pin 2: one step counter-clockwise from pin 1.
facts: Position: 1 pin counter-clockwise from the notch.
555 function: TRIGGER — pulling it low starts the timing cycle.

zones.summary: Pin 3: two steps counter-clockwise from pin 1.
facts: Position: 2 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
555 function: OUTPUT — this is the pin that drives your LED or buzzer.

zones.summary: Pin 4: the last pin along the bottom edge.
facts: Position: 3 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
555 function: RESET — hold it high for normal running; pull it low to force the output off.

zones.summary: Pin 5: the count turns the corner and comes back along the top edge.
facts: Position: 4 pins counter-clockwise from the notch — directly opposite pin 4.
555 function: CONTROL VOLTAGE — usually left alone, often with a small capacitor to ground.

zones.summary: Pin 6: continuing right to left along the top edge.
facts: Position: 5 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
555 function: THRESHOLD — when the voltage here rises high enough, the cycle ends.

zones.summary: Pin 7: second from the end of the top edge.
facts: Position: 6 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
555 function: DISCHARGE — it drains the timing capacitor to start the next cycle.

zones.summary: Pin 8: the last pin, sitting directly across the package from pin 1.
facts: Position: 7 pins counter-clockwise from the notch — right back beside where you started.
555 function: VCC, the positive supply.
Pin 8 and pin 1 are the supply pair, on opposite corners of the notch end.

zones.label: backwards?
zones.summary: Rotate the chip 180° and every pin lands somewhere it does not belong.
facts: Pin 1 (GND) would sit where pin 5 (CONTROL VOLTAGE) belongs, and pin 8 (VCC) would land on pin 4 (RESET).
Power and ground end up reversed across the chip — the one mistake most likely to destroy it.
This is why the notch matters: it is the only thing on the package telling you which end is which.

quiz.question: Which feature on the package tells you where pin 1 is?
quiz.explanation: The notch (and often a dimple beside pin 1) is the orientation marker.

quiz.question: Which pin is the positive supply, VCC, on a 555?
quiz.explanation: Pin 8 is VCC, sitting directly across the notch end from pin 1.

quiz.question: Which pin drives the load — the one you would wire your LED to?
Counting counter-clockwise from the notch, which pin comes immediately after pin 4?
quiz.explanation: The count turns the corner at pin 4 and continues with pin 5 on the top edge.

quiz.question: You seat the chip rotated 180 degrees. Where does pin 1 end up?
quiz.explanation: Pin 1 lands in pin 5's socket, and power and ground are reversed across the chip.
